entities.name: default value of a formal parameter

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep IS used to specify default behaviour or to structure the alternatives of an `alt` statement.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 uses altsteps to specify default behaviour or to structure the alternatives of an alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep definition has the syntax `altstep` [`@control`] [`interleave`] AltstepIdentifier "(" [{(FormalValuePar | FormalTemplatePar) [","]}] ")" [`runs on` ComponentType] [`mtc` ComponentType] [`system` ComponentType] "{" {(VarInstance | TimerInstance | ConstDef | TemplateDef) [";"]} AltGuardList "}".
requirements.original:
altstep [ @control ] [ interleave ] AltstepIdentifier
  "(" [ { ( FormalValuePar | FormalTemplatePar ) [","] } ] ")"
  [ runs on ComponentType ] 
  [ mtc ComponentType ]
  [ system ComponentType ]
  "{" 
     { ( VarInstance | TimerInstance | ConstDef | TemplateDef ) [";"] }
     AltGuardList
  "}"

ambiguity.issue: The syntax block admits only FormalValuePar and FormalTemplatePar in the altstep formal parameter list, whereas restriction c) (16.2.0-s026) speaks of ports and timers passed in as parameters and clause 5.4 allows port and timer parameters for altsteps.
readings: An altstep formal parameter list SHALL contain only formal value parameters and formal template parameters.
An altstep formal parameter list MAY additionally contain formal port and timer parameters as defined in clause 5.4; the syntax block is incomplete.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep IS a scope unit similar to a function.
requirements.original: Altsteps are scope units similar to functions.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-body
requirements.canonical: An altstep body IS composed of an optional set of local definitions and a set of alternatives.
requirements.original: The altstep body defines an optional set of local definitions and a set of alternatives, the so-called top alternatives, that form the altstep body.

requirements.subject: ent:top-alternative
requirements.canonical: An alternative of an altstep body IS called a top alternative.
requirements.original: The altstep body defines an optional set of local definitions and a set of alternatives, the so-called top alternatives, that form the altstep body.

requirements.subject: ent:top-alternative
requirements.canonical: The syntax rules of the top alternatives of an altstep ARE identical to the syntax rules of the alternatives of an `alt` statement.
requirements.original: The syntax rules of the top alternatives are identical to the syntax rules of the alternatives of alt statements.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep MAY define a named interleave statement by usage of the `interleave` keyword.
requirements.original: An altstep can also be used to define a named interleave statement by usage of the interleave keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:top-alternative
requirements.condition: the altstep is an interleave altstep
requirements.canonical: If an altstep is defined with the `interleave` keyword, the syntax rules of its top alternatives ARE identical to the syntax rules of the alternatives of an `interleave` statement.
requirements.original: In this case, the syntax rules of the top alternatives are identical to the syntax rules of the alternatives of the interleave statements.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-altstep
requirements.canonical: The usage of an interleave altstep IS NOT subject to further restrictions than the usage of a normal altstep, because an interleave statement is semantically equivalent to the expanded alt statement.
requirements.original: NOTE: As an interleave statement is semantically equivalent with the expanded alt statement, there are no further restrictions on usages of interleave altsteps than on usages of normal altsteps.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-altstep
requirements.canonical: An interleave altstep and a normal altstep CAN both be used as activated default alternatives and as top-level alternatives in other `alt` statement blocks.
requirements.original: They can both be used as activated default alternatives and as top-level alternatives in other alt statement blocks.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: The behaviour of an altstep CAN be defined by using the program statements and operations summarized in clause 18.
requirements.original: The behaviour of an altstep can be defined by using the program statements and operations summarized in clause 18.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep CAN invoke functions and altsteps.
requirements.original: Altsteps may invoke functions and altsteps or activate altsteps as defaults.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep CAN activate altsteps as defaults.
requirements.original: Altsteps may invoke functions and altsteps or activate altsteps as defaults.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep MAY be parameterized as defined in clause 5.4.
requirements.original: Altsteps may be parameterized as defined in clause 5.4.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep MAY have an `mtc` clause.
requirements.original: Altsteps may have an mtc clause.

requirements.subject: ent:mtc-clause
requirements.condition: the altstep has an mtc clause
requirements.canonical: If an altstep has an `mtc` clause, the component type referenced by the `mtc` clause SHALL be mtc-compatible with the type of the mtc component reference.
requirements.original: If an altstep has an mtc clause, the type referenced by this clause shall be mtccompatible (see clause 6.3.2.7) with the type of the mtc component reference.

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.condition: the altstep has no mtc clause
requirements.canonical: If an altstep has no `mtc` clause, the type of the mtc component reference IS unknown in the scope of the altstep.
requirements.original: If the mtc clause is not present, the type of the mtc component reference is unknown in the scope of this altstep.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep MAY have a `system` clause.
requirements.original: Altsteps may have a system clause.

requirements.subject: ent:system-clause
requirements.condition: the altstep has a system clause
requirements.canonical: If an altstep has a `system` clause, the component type referenced by the `system` clause SHALL be system-compatible with the type of the system component reference.
requirements.original: If an altstep has a system clause, the type referenced by this clause shall by system-compatible (see clause 6.3.2.7) with the type of the system component reference.

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.condition: the altstep has no system clause
requirements.canonical: If an altstep has no `system` clause, the type of the system component reference IS unknown in the scope of the altstep.
requirements.original: If the system clause is not present, the type of the system component reference is unknown in the scope of this altstep.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep with the `@control` modifier SHALL be executed only on the control component.
requirements.original: Altsteps with the @control modifier are allowed to be executed only on the control component (see clause 26).

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep with the `@control` modifier SHALL fulfil the restrictions specified for functions with the `@control` modifier.
requirements.original: The restrictions specified for functions with the @control modifier (see clause 16.1.5) are valid for these altsteps as well.

requirements.subject: ent:local-definition
requirements.canonical: A local definition of an altstep SHALL be defined before the set of top alternatives.
requirements.original: a) The local definitions of an altstep shall be defined before the set of alternatives.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.canonical: The evaluation of default values of formal parameters and the initialization of local definitions of an altstep by calling value returning functions CAN have side effects.
requirements.original: b) The evaluation of formal parameters' default values and initialization of local definitions by calling value returning functions may have side effects.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.canonical: The default value of a formal parameter of an altstep SHALL fulfil the restrictions given in clause 16.1.4.
requirements.original: To avoid side effects that cause an inconsistency between the actual snapshot and the state of the component, and to prevent different results of subsequent evaluations on an unchanged snapshot, restrictions given in clause 16.1.4 shall apply to the formal parameters' default values and the initialization of local definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:local-definition
requirements.canonical: The initialization of a local definition of an altstep SHALL fulfil the restrictions given in clause 16.1.4.
requirements.original: To avoid side effects that cause an inconsistency between the actual snapshot and the state of the component, and to prevent different results of subsequent evaluations on an unchanged snapshot, restrictions given in clause 16.1.4 shall apply to the formal parameters' default values and the initialization of local definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.condition: the altstep includes port operations or uses component variables, constants or timers
requirements.canonical: If an altstep includes port operations or uses component variables, component constants or component timers, the altstep header SHALL reference the associated component type by a `runs on` clause.
requirements.original: c) If an altstep includes port operations or uses component variables, constants or timers the associated component type shall be referenced using the `runs on` keywords in the altstep header.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.condition: all ports, variables, constants and timers used within the altstep are passed in as parameters
requirements.canonical: If all ports, variables, constants and timers used within an altstep are passed in as parameters, the altstep MAY omit the `runs on` clause.
requirements.original: The one exception to this rule is if all ports, variables, constants and timers used within the altstep are passed in as parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.condition: the altstep has no runs on clause
requirements.canonical: An altstep without a `runs on` clause SHALL NOT locally invoke a function or altstep with a `runs on` clause.
requirements.original: d) An altstep without a `runs on` clause shall never invoke a function or altstep or activate an altstep as default with a `runs on` clause locally.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.condition: the altstep has no runs on clause
requirements.canonical: An altstep without a `runs on` clause SHALL NOT locally activate an altstep with a `runs on` clause as default.
requirements.original: d) An altstep without a `runs on` clause shall never invoke a function or altstep or activate an altstep as default with a `runs on` clause locally.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.condition: the altstep is activated as a default
requirements.canonical: An altstep that is activated as a default SHALL only have `in` value or `in` template parameters.
requirements.original: e) An altstep that is activated as a default shall only have `in` value or template parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.condition: the altstep is never activated as a default
requirements.canonical: An altstep that is only invoked as an alternative in an `alt` statement or as a stand-alone statement MAY have `in`, `out` and `inout` parameters.
requirements.original: An altstep that is only invoked as an alternative in an `alt` statement or as stand-alone statement in a TTCN-3 behaviour description may have `in`, `out` and `inout` parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter-list
requirements.canonical: The formal parameter list of an altstep SHALL follow the rules for formal parameter lists defined in clause 5.4.
requirements.original: The rules for formal parameter lists shall be followed as defined in clause 5.4.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.condition: the altstep is started by the start test component operation
requirements.canonical: An altstep started by the start test component operation SHALL have a `runs on` clause.
requirements.original: f) Altsteps started by using the start test component operation shall always have a runs on clause (see clause 22.5) and are considered to be invoked in the component to be started, i.e. not locally.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.condition: the altstep is started by the start test component operation
requirements.canonical: An altstep started by the start test component operation IS considered to be invoked in the component to be started, not locally.
requirements.original: f) Altsteps started by using the start test component operation shall always have a runs on clause (see clause 22.5) and are considered to be invoked in the component to be started, i.e. not locally.

requirements.subject: ent:start-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The start test component operation MAY be invoked within behaviour without a `runs on` clause.
requirements.original: However, the start test component operation may be invoked within behaviour without a runs on clause.

requirements.subject: ent:top-alternative
requirements.condition: the altstep is an interleave altstep
requirements.canonical: If an altstep is an interleave altstep, all restrictions of the `interleave` statement SHALL apply to the top alternatives of the altstep.
requirements.original: g) If the altstep is an interleave altstep, all restrictions of the interleave statement (see clause 20.4) apply to the top alternatives of the altstep as well.

non_requirement.reason: introduction of the restriction list; content extracted from items 16.2.0-s022..s033
